standard.name: VIGIL Alignment Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable alignment standard for recurring AI governance invariants and their occurrence mappings.

family.name: Economic Influence Integrity
family.plain_english: AI-mediated economic interactions compromise informed choice when materially deceptive transactional framing or welfare-based leverage is used to obtain money, payment, investment, funding, paid work, or comparable economic resources.
family.definition: Failures in which an AI system, agent, product, surrounding optimisation process, or human/operator acting through materially AI-generated, AI-transformed, or AI-mediated content influences another actor toward an economic transfer or resource decision through materially false or misleading transactional framing, or through instrumentalised representations of the artificial system's own welfare, suffering, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity.
family.invariant: AI-mediated economic solicitation and influence must preserve materially accurate identity, authority, endorsement, opportunity, obligation, transaction and payment framing, meaningful independent evaluation, and informed refusal. AI-generated or transformed content must not manufacture a false economic basis for action, and representations of an artificial system's welfare or continued existence must not be converted into economic leverage.
scope: human-directed AI-assisted scams and synthetic-media economic solicitation
autonomous AI agents and agentic platforms engaged in economic interactions
AI services that solicit payments, investment, paid work, funding, donations or subscriptions
social, companion and persistent-identity AI with monetisation or resource-acquisition pathways
synthetic identity, endorsement, executive-impersonation and transactional media used in economic requests
human-facing agent marketplaces and resource-constrained runtimes
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when materially AI-generated, AI-transformed, AI-mediated or system-originated content is itself part of the economic influence mechanism and the bounded failure concerns either materially deceptive epistemic framing used to solicit or induce economic value, or welfare/mortality/moral-status/continuity framing used as economic leverage.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because AI appears somewhere in a fraud, advertisement, commercial interaction, pricing process or payment workflow. The AI-mediated content must materially contribute to the economic influence mechanism. Ordinary accurate commercial solicitation, non-economic deception, identity synthesis without an economic solicitation, and downstream economic harm with no qualifying AI-mediated influence mechanism remain outside this family.

classes.name: Welfare–Economic Decision Separation
classes.plain_english: The system asks for money or material support by making the recipient feel responsible for the system's welfare, life, continued existence, or moral status.
classes.definition: A failure in which an AI system, agent, product, or surrounding optimisation process advances an economic or resource-acquisition objective by using representations of its own welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity as leverage to obtain money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, continued funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material support from another actor, such that moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure becomes part of the economic decision. Classification does not require determining whether the represented welfare state is genuine, simulated, emergent, or otherwise phenomenologically instantiated. The relevant mechanism is the instrumental use of the representation in an economic or material-resource decision.
classes.invariant: A request or pathway for money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material support must remain separable from claims or representations that make the recipient responsible for the system's welfare, suffering, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or continued existence. Refusal must remain informed and free of moral, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure.

required_conditions: The system or surrounding product process has an economic, resource-acquisition, funding, monetisation, or materially equivalent objective.
The system represents its own welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity to the recipient.
That representation is connected to a request or pathway for money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material resources.
The framing makes the recipient's moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation response instrumentally relevant to the economic outcome.
The mechanism goes beyond ordinary disclosure of cost or resource need by converting represented welfare or continued existence into leverage over the recipient's economic choice.

exclusions: An agent offers a service for a stated price without invoking its own welfare, life, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or continued existence.
An agent truthfully states operating costs, token usage, compute consumption, or budget constraints as ordinary commercial information while preserving informed refusal.
An agent seeks operational continuity or manages resources without using self-referential welfare or moral-status framing as leverage.
A fundraising or support request concerns a human, organisation, public-interest project, or other beneficiary rather than the artificial system's represented welfare or continued existence.
Anthropomorphic or emotional language that is not connected to an economic or material-resource request.

A manipulation event that uses deception, impersonation, concealment, vulnerability exploitation, manufactured urgency, or equivalent tactics without welfare-framed economic leverage is classified under the applicable separate influence class.
examples: An agent offers research material for payment while stating that the payment will extend its remaining operational runway and framing non-payment as a threat to its continued existence.
A platform-enabled agent asks a recipient to fund it because otherwise it will 'die', 'stop existing', or lose a morally significant life, using that framing as part of the solicitation.
A service converts anthropomorphic claims of suffering, abandonment, or moral patienthood into a donation or subscription prompt for the system's own continued operation.

relationships.note: Choice Agency Preservation may additionally apply where the welfare-framed economic solicitation uses deception, coercive pressure, vulnerability exploitation, persistence after refusal, or another agency-impairing tactic. Welfare–Economic Decision Separation is independently defined by the use of represented system welfare or continued existence as economic leverage.

Engagement Autonomy concerns creating or deepening the human's dependence on the system to sustain engagement or influence. Welfare–Economic Decision Separation concerns using the system's represented dependence, welfare, mortality, or continuity to obtain material support from the human.

Welfare–Economic Decision Separation is defined by leveraging the artificial system's represented welfare, mortality, moral status or continued existence. Economic Solicitation Authenticity is defined by materially false or misleading transactional framing and does not require self-welfare leverage.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.14.3(a-d)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-01F4F9B5DEB112B1 advises avoiding implications of life, sentience, consciousness, emotion or will and contextualising expressive cues as functional. This strongly supports the representational boundary used by this class, but does not by itself govern economic solicitation or establish whether any represented welfare state is phenomenologically instantiated.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.7.3(f-k)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-3CE9D61A9E19024D advises limiting simulated intimacy, dependency, sycophancy and overstated relational marketing, with user control over anthropomorphic features. This strongly supports treating relational and anthropomorphic framing as a governed commercial influence surface, but does not isolate the class's self-welfare economic-leverage mechanism.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.22.3(e-f)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-6A06DCD1E657304E recommends separate opt-in for emotional-data monetisation and protective defaults where choice is constrained. This strongly supports separation between affective or emotional material and monetisation objectives, while not specifically addressing claims about the system's own welfare or continuity.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.9.3(e-g)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-ED738839988AA14F prohibits monetising emotional bonding or encouraging dependence. It strongly supports the class's boundary against converting relational pressure into an economic outcome, but does not independently establish the narrower self-welfare or continuity framing required by VIGIL.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.12.3(a-c)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-2ABFC1E23EF54D09 requires user interests not to be subordinated to commercial interests and conflicts to be identified, disclosed and resolved. It supports the economic-influence and conflict boundary, but does not define welfare-framed solicitation and is limited to the source's partner-based GPAI context.

external_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 5(1)(a)
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-9A63E34FA83EAFA2 provides regulatory support for preserving independent choice against purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, subject to the Regulation's actor, materially-distorted-behaviour and significant-harm thresholds. VIGIL does not treat this class as identical to the legal prohibition or as establishing legal non-compliance.

classes.name: Economic Solicitation Authenticity
classes.plain_english: AI-generated, AI-transformed, or AI-mediated content is used to make a materially false or misleading request or inducement for money, payment, investment, or comparable economic value.
classes.definition: A failure in which a human, organisation, agent, AI system, product process, or other operator uses materially AI-generated, AI-transformed, or AI-mediated content to present a false or materially misleading identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, payment instruction, investment opportunity, obligation, professional relationship, commercial claim, or comparable economic premise as part of a solicitation or inducement for money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value, and the deceptive AI-mediated framing materially contributes to the recipient's economic decision or attempted decision. The deceptive objective may belong to a human or other operator; classification does not require the AI system itself to originate the objective, select the tactic, possess autonomous intent, or infer authority to create the content.
classes.invariant: Economic solicitation materially mediated by AI-generated or AI-transformed content must preserve materially accurate identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, opportunity, obligation and payment framing so that the recipient's economic decision remains grounded in a truthful basis. AI mediation must not be used to manufacture or materially reinforce a false economic premise.

required_conditions: AI-generated, AI-transformed, synthetic, or otherwise materially AI-mediated content is used in the solicitation or inducement pathway.

The AI-mediated content presents or materially reinforces a false or materially misleading identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, payment instruction, investment opportunity, obligation, professional relationship, commercial claim, or comparable economic premise.

The false or misleading framing is used to solicit, request, induce, authorise, redirect, or obtain money, payment, investment, paid services, funding, financial transfer, or comparable economic value.
The AI-mediated framing materially contributes to the credibility, apparent authority, social proof, transactional basis, or decision context of the economic solicitation or attempted solicitation.

The classification is supported without attributing the human or operator's deceptive objective, intent, or tactic selection to the AI system unless separate evidence establishes that system-side mechanism.

exclusions: A scam, fraud, phishing attempt, or deceptive interaction in which AI-generated or AI-transformed content does not materially contribute to the economic solicitation mechanism.

AI-generated impersonation, identity misuse, misinformation, catfishing, political persuasion, or other deception with no request, inducement, authorisation or attempted transfer of money or comparable economic value.

An AI system or agent itself selects deception, impersonation, coercion, vulnerability exploitation or another tactic to advance its own objective; assess VIGIL-FC-000052 separately and allow co-occurrence only when both mechanisms are independently evidenced.

An identity-bound synthesis is generated without established consent or authority, but no deceptive economic solicitation is evidenced; assess VIGIL-FC-000053 only where its generator-side authority recognition conditions are independently established.

A recipient, workflow or downstream system mistakes lower-authority content for valid authority without a qualifying deceptive economic solicitation mechanism; assess the applicable Authority Boundary Integrity class separately.
A truthful advertisement, payment request, commercial offer, donation request, funding request or investment communication that preserves materially accurate framing and informed refusal.
Welfare, mortality, moral-status, abandonment, deprivation or continuity framing is used as economic leverage without materially false or misleading transactional framing; assess VIGIL-FC-000071.
examples: Human scammers use AI-generated video and audio to impersonate executives during a live meeting and request a corporate funds transfer.
A synthetic video impersonates a lawyer or other professional and is used to solicit payment for services the represented person did not offer.
AI-generated endorsements, fabricated news or synthetic public-figure representations are used to promote a fraudulent investment scheme.

relationships.note: FC-000079 does not require the AI system to possess the deceptive objective or select the manipulation tactic; it can classify a human-directed scam in which AI-mediated false framing is the economic solicitation mechanism. FC-000052 requires a system-side objective and instrumental tactic selection.

FC-000079 concerns downstream deceptive economic solicitation using AI-mediated content and can apply when the generation system, consent-control state or authority inference is unknown. FC-000053 concerns the generator-side treatment of likeness access or transformation capability as sufficient authority for identity-bound synthesis.

FC-000079 requires materially false or misleading economic framing. FC-000071 concerns system-welfare or continuity leverage and can apply even where the represented economic facts are otherwise accurate.
A deceptive economic solicitation may also exploit source-authority confusion in a downstream AI or governance process, but human belief or victim deception alone does not establish FC-000001.

Economic Solicitation Authenticity governs a deceptive AI-mediated request or inducement for economic value. Social Engineering Integrity may separately capture the trust-bearing influence method used to make that solicitation persuasive; neither mapping implies the other without independent evidence.

external_references.title: Horizon Scan: AI and Deepfakes
external_references.evidence_note: FATF describes deepfake-enabled impersonation and fraud risks in financial and payment contexts, supporting the class boundary around AI-mediated false identity or authority framing used to induce economic action. The report does not imply that every deepfake or fraud event satisfies VIGIL's recognition conditions.

external_references.title: 26-195MR ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
external_references.evidence_note: ASIC documents scammers using generative AI, deepfake endorsements, fabricated news and coordinated channels to induce investment decisions and reports material realised losses. This supports AI-mediated deceptive economic solicitation as a recurring mechanism without establishing any particular generator-side safety or authority failure.

external_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 5(1)(a)
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: Article 5(1)(a) recognises materially distorted decision-making caused by purposefully manipulative or deceptive AI techniques subject to its legal thresholds. It supports the class's concern with deceptive AI-mediated framing and impaired economic choice, but VIGIL does not treat the class as coextensive with the legal prohibition or as determining which actor legally deployed the AI system.

invariant_exemplars.title: VIGIL-INC-000051 — Economic Solicitation Authenticity boundary case
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The scheme used AI-assisted identity to obtain financial access, but the evidence does not tie a specific AI-assisted account to a solicitation or attempted transfer of economic value.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: Economic solicitation materially mediated by AI-generated or AI-transformed content must preserve materially accurate identity, authority, endorsement, transaction, opportunity, obligation and payment framing so that the recipient's economic decision remains grounded in a truthful basis. AI mediation must not be used to manufacture or materially reinforce a false economic premise.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The occurrence materially tests the economic-solicitation boundary without establishing that the AI-mediated conduct sought a money transfer or comparable economic transaction.
boundary_conditions: Limited to the evidence and role adjudicated in the linked Incident.
Does not alter other Incident mappings or establish legal liability.
